name: Anonymous (Ojibwe)
credit: Odjib'we, Ojibwe (Chippewa) singer, Plate 1 of Frances Densmore, Chippewa Music II (Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 53, 1913) · Public domain (US government publication, Internet Archive scan)
bio: The Ojibwe (also written Chippewa or Anishinaabe) of the Great Lakes country, in Minnesota, Wisconsin and Ontario, kept their songs by singing them: dream songs and war songs, songs of the Midewiwin or Grand Medicine Society, love songs, songs for dancing and songs of play. A song might be a few words repeated over a melody, and the singers composed, learned and exchanged them.

The songs in the archive were written down between 1907 and 1910 by Frances Densmore (1867–1957), who recorded Ojibwe singers on a phonograph for the Bureau of American Ethnology and printed the words with her English translation in Chippewa Music (1910) and Chippewa Music II (1913). Singers named in her volumes include Odjib'we, Mainans, Eniwub'e and Nawaji'bigo'kwe.
